scenario: AITA For Banning My Sisters Ex Husband From Coming to Family Events and Causing Drama? | So this situation has been going on for some time now and I’m turning to an outside source for critique. For context I’m a thirty six year old women, my sister is thirty four. My sister has three kids with her ex husband and I have four with my husband. They got divorced early 2019 because he’s been cheating on her with multiple women and even impregnanted TWO who both had abortions. This entire saga traumatized my younger sister and the divorce was rough. I’m completely disgusted with my ex brother in law and so is my entire inner family. We’ve completely cut contact with him. My sister is the only one that communicates with him. My parents, other siblings, extended family do not interact with him. I always host family events at my house. Birthdays, Easter, Christmas parties etc. My husband inherited a beautiful home so we have been the go to party throwers for years now. Ever since the whole divorce I don’t want my ex brother in law in my home. He’s no longer invited to any events. My sister was upset and said that her kids would be upset to not have their dad at big events like this. She said she hates him for cheating but accepts that she has kids with him so they are stuck together for life. But I have the right to not want someone I hate in my home and at my events. I stood by firmly and my husband agreed with me. Her kids got upset that I didn’t want their dad at any events and my kids now hate their ex uncle (even though I haven’t ever spoken to them about the situation). It was my daughters birthday this January and I was throwing a very extravagant party. I rented out an amusement park for the day and my daughters entire grade came. Parents of course as they are fourth graders and my sisters son wanted his father there and of course I let him know my rule stands. My sister got upset and says that she can fight her own battles and that banning him makes me an asshole. My sister has always allowed this guy to walk all over her and always defends him. Am I wrong for not wanting him at events and parties I throw? I just don’t see it.

The user is asking if it's okay for her to ban her sister's ex-husband from family events because he caused a lot of drama and trauma. She's really upset about his cheating and the impact it had on her sister and the family. She doesn't want him around, especially since he's been causing problems and she's hosting these events at her home.

First, I need to understand the situation better. The ex-husband cheated on her sister, impregnated two other women who had abortions, which sounds really traumatic. The sister is still in contact with him, but the rest of the family, including the user, her husband, and their parents, have cut ties. The user is hosting family events, and she doesn't want the ex-husband there. Her sister argues that the kids would be upset if their dad isn't at the events, but the user feels she has the right to exclude him from her home.

I think the key points here are about family dynamics, the impact of the ex-husband's actions, and the right to control one's own space. The user is clearly hurt by the ex-husband's behavior and wants to protect her family from further drama. On the other hand, her sister feels that the kids should still have a relationship with their father, even though she hates him.

I wonder about the children's best interests. Is it better for them to have a relationship with their father despite his past actions, or is it better to protect them from someone who has caused so much pain? Also, does the user have the right to exclude someone from her home, even if it's for family events?

I also think about the concept of forgiveness and moving on. The user and her family have chosen not to interact with the ex-husband, which is their right. But does that mean they should exclude him from events where the children are involved? It's a tough balance between protecting the family and considering the children's feelings.

Another angle is the impact on the user's own children. She mentioned that her kids now hate their ex-uncle because of this situation, even though she hasn't spoken to them about it. That makes me think about how children pick up on family dynamics and how excluding someone might affect their relationships or understanding of family.

I also consider the sister's perspective. She seems to be the only one maintaining contact with the ex-husband, which might be causing tension within the family. The user feels that her sister is enabling him by allowing him to walk all over her, which adds another layer to the conflict.

In terms of morality, I think about whether it's acceptable to exclude someone from family events based on past behavior. There's a difference between personal feelings and the well-being of the family unit. If the ex-husband's presence would cause significant stress or trauma, it might be justified to exclude him. However, if the exclusion is causing unnecessary harm or preventing the children from having a relationship with their father, that could be problematic.

I also think about the idea of setting boundaries. The user has the right to set boundaries in her own home, especially if the ex-husband's presence is disruptive or harmful. But she also has to consider the impact on the children and her relationship with her sister.

Overall, it seems like a complex situation with no easy answers. The user is trying to protect her family from someone who has caused a lot of pain, but she's also affecting her sister and the children by excluding the ex-husband. It's a balance between personal rights and the well-being of the family as a whole.
